Subject: Manager handback + sensitive routing — options and ask

Team,

I put together a lean proposal for how we handle manager handbacks and the routing of sensitive review cases this cycle. High-level asks: review the two routing options (A = centralized People Ops handoff, B = delegated manager routing with legal oversight), flag any compliance blockers, and confirm the timeline below so I can lock invites.

Quick summary:
- Goal: ensure sensitive cases (execs, people on PIP, privacy/data-exposed roles) are handled with minimal leakage and predictable approval steps.
- Option A: People Ops triage -> legal review -> manager follow-up (simpler for audit trails).
- Option B: Manager triage with required encrypted handback sheet and People Ops spot-checks (scales better, needs tooling).

Proposed timeline (draft):
- June 22: Managers receive templates and triage rubric
- July 6: Manager handbacks due for first cohort
- July 20: Calibration + case escalations resolved

Attachments: manager_handback_template_v1.docx, sensitive-routing-matrix.xlsx, external-comm-templates.md (stubs attached to this thread).

Open questions:
1) Do we need an explicit stamping step from Legal before manager outreach to employees in Option A?
2) For Option B, can we rely on redaction + encrypted handback or do we need a formal People Ops approval ticket?

Please reply with decisions or comments by EOD Wednesday so I can finalize the calendar and templates.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Agree with Stephanie on leaning Option A for the pilot. A couple of additional items:

- Legal run: I'll ask Legal to pre-clear the stamping language, but we should avoid language that reads like a disciplinary conclusion — keep it factual.
- Communications: add a short triage FAQ for managers (one pager) so they know when to escalate.
- Metrics: People Ops to track time-to-resolution and number of escalations; include a column in the routing matrix.

Note on timelines: June 29 for manager handbacks feels tight for some larger teams. Propose a tiered deadline: small teams (<=8) due June 29; large teams due July 6. That will reduce noisy follow-ups.

I'll loop Legal and confirm when I have their preliminary sign-off.

Diego — good start. A couple practical notes from the manager enablement side:

- Redaction: we should provide a quick redaction checklist (PII, health info, investigative details). Managers often over-share; a checklist will help.
- Forms: can we make the handback a fillable form (PDF) that automatically masks employee IDs? That avoids accidental exports.
- Training: 30-minute optional sync for managers the week after templates land. I'll own scheduling.

Also, for the external comms templates, add a version for partner contacts (we sometimes have joint accounts where comms must be aligned).

Thanks — Monica
Manager, Enablement (People)
Redwood Inference

Diego/Team — external consultant chiming in with two practical items from other customers:

1) Use a short, machine-readable tag on handback files (e.g., SENSITIVE:LEGAL) so downstream tooling can auto-route.
2) Keep the manager-facing comms extremely prescriptive — exact subject lines and script snippets reduce risk.

Happy to draft both if useful; can send a short pack by EOD.

—Ari
Talentworks (external)
